messages:
intrusion-bot: [P1 ALERT] Suspicious image/digest on prod cluster (prod-us-east-1). ReplicaSet=api-frontend. Expected digest sha256:0a1b2c... but node pulled sha256:9f8e7d.... Pod started with securityContext.privileged=true. Audit log shows image pull by serviceaccount: frontend-deployer-sa at 11:13 UTC. Possible image tampering or CI/CD compromise. Logs + event: https://internal/logs/1750254821

priya shah: I'm taking lead. Marking incident INC-2025-042. Containment steps coming now. Cordon node where suspect pod is running and scale down RS.

ryan-oncall: cordoning node node-prod-37 now. running: `kubectl cordon node-prod-37` && `kubectl drain node-prod-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

samir: good. also killing the affected pods and forcing recreate from registry digest we verify. `kubectl delete pod -l app=api-frontend -n prod`

elaine: copying image digests from CI: we have signed digest 0a1b2c... from our internal registry (gcr.redwood-inference). The pulled digest 9f8e7d... is not signed by our COSIGN key. Suspicious.

jordan: running cosign verify locally against the suspect image. command: ```cosign verify --key k8s://projects/redwood/keys/cosign public gcr.io/redwood/api@sha256:9f8e7d...``` getting VERIFICATION FAILED

mike: scanning the node for other tampered images and binaries. `runc list` and `ps aux` look for unexpected containers/processes. also snapshot node disk for forensics.

priya shah: good checklist. Samir, hold on rolling updates until we confirm clean images. Ryan, keep node cordoned. Elaine, pull CI artifact and re-push to a quarantine registry for analysis.

samir: copying artifacts to quarantine registry now. `gcloud auth configure-docker` then `docker pull gcr.io/redwood/api@sha256:0a1b2c...` -> `docker tag ... quarantine-registry.redwood/api:suspect-1750254821` -> `docker push ...`

intrusion-bot: Audit snippet: `kube-audit: verb=create, user=sa:frontend-deployer-sa, object=pods, timestamp=2025-11-06T11:12:49Z, attr=image=registry.hub.docker.com/redwood/api:stable`

elaine: serviceaccount tokens rotated 2 days ago as part of release. Need to check CI pipeline creds — maybe compromised. Also check if KMS key used for signing was used unexpectedly.

mike: quick RBAC sweep: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects[]?.name=="frontend-deployer-sa")'` shows frontend-deployer-sa bound to cluster-admin via legacy binding `ci-deployers-binding`. WTF.

samir: that's the root cause then. CI SA has excessive privileges. I will remove cluster-admin binding and create a least-privilege role for deployments.

ryan-oncall: creating a temporary RBAC guard: `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding ci-deployers-binding` (paused) — will do only after we ensure no more pending deploys. Anyone object?

elaine: do it. We need to limit blast radius. We should also rotate the KMS key used for signing and revoke prior cosign keys.

priya shah: agreed. Action list so far: 1) cordon + drain node-prod-37 (ryan) 2) kill suspect pods (samir) 3) quarantine image and forensic scan (elaine/mike) 4) remove cluster-admin binding for CI SA (samir) 5) rotate cosign/KMS keys and rotate CI tokens (elaine) 6) prepare customer comms if needed (priya). Owner tags in ticket.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2025-042 created and linked: https://internal/incidents/INC-2025-042. Priority P1. Pager duty notified.

jordan: follow-up verification: run `cosign verify-blob` against the quarantined artifact and send to malware scanning team. Also check container runtime logs for `setns` syscalls indicating possible escape attempts.

mike: forensics snapshot done. pulled `/var/lib/docker/image/*` + kernel dmesg logs. No obvious rce but there are writes to `/tmp/.X11` odd. collecting strace dumps.

priya shah: rolling communications: Notifying CISO and legal. We are not notifying customers yet until we know scope. Draft comms in INC ticket.

samir: RBAC change applied: removed ci-deployers-binding. Created `deployment-limited-role` with minimal perms and bound to `frontend-deployer-sa`. Pushed to gitops and locked deploy pipeline.

elaine: rotated cosign key and revoked old signature key. KMS rotation started — will take up to 1h to propagate. Also invalidated CI tokens and kicked all runners.

ryan-oncall: uncordoning other nodes after scan; keeping node-prod-37 cordoned until forensics signoff. `kubectl uncordon node-prod-35` etc.

intrusion-bot: Additional detection: suspicious outbound traffic to 198.51.100.77 from node-prod-37 at 11:18 UTC. Network team notified to block IP.

priya shah: next steps after containment: 1) full postmortem 2) permanent RBAC policy enforcement (OPA/Gatekeeper) 3) sign-only-from-KMS workflow for images 4) CI least privilege audit 5) automated audit logging dashboard for image digest mismatches. Assign owners in ticket.

mike: opening a vuln triage for the image contents — malware team will confirm if binary modifications were malicious.

jordan: suggest adding a kube admission webhook to reject privileged pods unless explicitly allowed. I'll draft PR.

samir: happy to pick up the RBAC hardening PR and the gatekeeper policy.

priya shah: thanks everyone. Stand down once KMS rotation + forensics confirm no further compromise. We'll schedule a 90-min postmortem tomorrow.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2025-042 status: CONTAINED. See ticket for playbooks and artifacts.

elaine: quick note — we found a misconfigured mirror step in CI that allowed unsigned images to be pulled from dockerhub if primary registry unavailable. Fix in flight.

mike: adding remediation checklist to the ticket and owners. Closing Slack thread for now, continue updates in INC-2025-042. :lock:
